Tuning context length with rolling-origin resampling

Source: vignettes/rolling-origin-tuning.Rmd
rolling-origin-tuning.Rmd

How much history should a foundation model condition on? More context is not always better — it can dilute recent signal and cost compute. Because zukzeit exposes context_length as a tunable dials parameter, you can answer this empirically with the standard tidymodels tuning machinery over rolling-origin (time-aware) resamples, rather than random cross-validation that would leak the future into the past.

The code below uses the executable stub fixture to demonstrate the mechanics, and every output is produced when this vignette is built. It is not a foundation-model benchmark: the stub forecasts the last observed value, so its score cannot depend on how much history it keeps. Repeat the workflow with TimesFM for a result that means something.

Some history to search over 

library(zukzeit)

set.seed(20260904)
months <- seq(as.Date("2015-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 96)
history <- data.frame(
  store = "north",
  month = months,
  sales = 100 + 0.8 * seq_along(months) +
    10 * sin(seq_along(months) * pi / 6) + rnorm(length(months), sd = 2)
)
head(history, 3)
#>   store      month    sales
#> 1 north 2015-01-01 103.2887
#> 2 north 2015-02-01 112.1575
#> 3 north 2015-03-01 113.0156

The spec

Mark context_length for tuning; everything else is fixed through the engine:

library(parsnip)
library(workflows)
library(tune)
library(dials)
#> Loading required package: scales
library(rsample)

spec <- zuk_reg(context_length = tune()) |>
  set_engine("zukzeit",
             model_id = "stub",
             index    = "month",
             id       = "store")

wf <- workflow() |>
  add_variables(outcomes = sales, predictors = c(month, store)) |>
  add_model(spec)

add_variables() matters here. index and id name columns the engine reads out of the data it is handed, and add_formula() keeps only the terms in the formula — which drops store before the engine sees it, and the fit then fails on a missing column.

Rolling-origin resamples

rsample::sliding_period() builds analysis/assessment splits that always move forward in time — the assessment window is strictly after its analysis window:

folds <- sliding_period(
  history,
  index       = month,
  period      = "year",
  lookback    = Inf,   # expanding origin: all history up to each split
  assess_stop = 1      # score one year ahead
)
folds
#> # Sliding period resampling 
#> # A tibble: 7 × 2
#>   splits          id    
#>   <list>          <chr> 
#> 1 <split [12/12]> Slice1
#> 2 <split [24/12]> Slice2
#> 3 <split [36/12]> Slice3
#> 4 <split [48/12]> Slice4
#> 5 <split [60/12]> Slice5
#> 6 <split [72/12]> Slice6
#> 7 <split [84/12]> Slice7

Search

Give context_length a range and let tune_grid() score each candidate:

grid <- grid_regular(context_length(range = c(12L, 60L)), levels = 4)

res <- tune_grid(
  wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid      = grid,
  metrics   = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::mae)
)

show_best(res, metric = "rmse")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   context_length .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config        
#>            <int> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1             12 rmse    standard    7.57     7   0.400 pre0_mod1_post0
#> 2             28 rmse    standard    7.57     7   0.400 pre0_mod2_post0
#> 3             44 rmse    standard    7.57     7   0.400 pre0_mod3_post0
#> 4             60 rmse    standard    7.57     7   0.400 pre0_mod4_post0
best <- select_best(res, metric = "rmse")
best
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   context_length .config        
#>            <int> <chr>          
#> 1             12 pre0_mod1_post0

final_fit <- finalize_workflow(wf, best) |>
  fit(data = history)
final_fit
#> ══ Workflow [trained] ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#> Preprocessor: Variables
#> Model: zuk_reg()
#> 
#> ── Preprocessor ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Outcomes: sales
#> Predictors: c(month, store)
#> 
#> ── Model ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> <zuk_fit> ("stub")
#> target "..y" over 1 series
#> <zuk_fit> ("stub")
#> target "..y" over 1 series

finalize_workflow() substitutes the chosen value back into the spec through the specification’s update() method, and the refit engine then keeps only that much history.

Notes

  • context_length bounds the most recent history retained by each fitted engine; the end-to-end behavior is covered with the stub in package tests.
  • The heavy per-candidate cost is inference, not training (these are zero-shot models), so keep the grid small and prefer sliding_period() windows that reflect your real forecast horizon.
  • Scores that are identical across the grid, as above, mean the model is not actually using the extra history — which for the stub is the correct answer, and for a real checkpoint is a finding worth investigating.
